---
title: "Quarto"
jupyter: php
---

Render a `.qmd` document with PHP cells by naming the kernel in its front
matter. No Quarto extension or other configuration is needed.

## A minimal document

````markdown
---
title: "Highway mileage"
jupyter: php
---

```{{php}}
$mpg = \Phibble\DataFrame::fromCsv('mpg.csv');
$mpg;
```
````

- `jupyter: php` names the kernel by the `--name` that `juphyter install` was
  given. `php` is the default, and a kernel installed with `--name php85` is
  named `jupyter: php85`.
- A cell is a fenced block whose info string is `{php}`. It holds PHP without
  an opening tag.
- Quarto runs the cells in order, in one PHP session per render.

Render it:

```bash
quarto render report.qmd
```

This writes `report.html` beside the document. `--to` chooses another format,
such as `--to typst` for a PDF.

Quarto runs its Jupyter engine in a Python interpreter of its own choosing,
which needs Jupyter in it. `juphyter doctor` reports whether it has one, and
[Python interpreters and editors](python.qmd) covers how to choose it. This
page was checked with Quarto 1.10.18, the version CI tests.

## Output formats

| Format | Command | Extra requirement |
|---|---|---|
| HTML | `quarto render report.qmd` | None. |
| PDF through Typst | `quarto render report.qmd --to typst` | [vl-convert](https://github.com/vega/vl-convert/releases) for phiz plots. |
| PDF through LaTeX | `quarto render report.qmd --to pdf` | vl-convert for phiz plots, and `rsvg-convert` from librsvg. |
| Word | `quarto render report.qmd --to docx` | vl-convert for phiz plots. Without `rsvg-convert`, Pandoc warns and embeds the SVG as it is. |

Typst ships inside Quarto and is the simpler PDF route. vl-convert produces
the static SVG of a phiz plot. Put it on `PATH`, or point `PHIZ_VL_CONVERT` at
it. Without it a plot has no SVG, and a PDF or Word document has no figure.

What each format takes from a cell's output:

| Format | A phiz plot | A phibble data frame |
|---|---|---|
| `html` | The interactive chart, drawn by Vega-Lite in the browser. | The HTML table, with the dimensions and the type row. |
| `typst`, `pdf` | The static SVG, as a numbered figure. | A typeset table, without the dimension note and the truncation footer. |
| `ipynb` | The HTML embed. | Nothing. |

`quarto render --to ipynb` converts the rendered document, and Quarto's
conversion drops HTML tables and error outputs. Render to HTML or PDF when a
document's tables matter.

## Cell options

Quarto's cell options are `#|` comments at the top of a cell. PHP reads them
as line comments.

```{php}
#| echo: false
use Phibble\DataFrame;
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;
```

- `#| echo: false` runs the cell and hides its source.
- `#| eval: false` shows the source and does not run it.
- `#| output: false` runs the cell and shows no output.
- `#| error: true` continues the render past a cell that throws, and keeps
  the traceback.
- `#| fig-cap: "..."` captions the cell's figure.
- `#| label: fig-mileage` gives the figure a cross-reference label.

A captioned plot:

```{php}
#| fig-cap: "City against highway mileage."
Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())->aes(x: 'cty', y: 'hwy')->point(opacity: 0.5);
```

## Projects and autoloading

Quarto runs the kernel in the document's directory. The kernel looks upward
from there for `vendor/autoload.php`, so a document inside a Composer project
can use that project's classes and packages. A document outside any project
names an autoloader with `JUPHYTER_AUTOLOAD` or a `juphyter.json` beside it.
[Which classes a notebook sees](install.qmd#which-classes-a-notebook-sees)
lists both.

In a Quarto project, each document names its kernel in its own front matter.

## Freeze

`execute: freeze: auto` works with PHP documents. Quarto re-executes a document
only when its source changes and stores the output in `_freeze/`. A project
that commits that directory can be rendered without the packages the cells
use, as long as a kernel with the document's name is registered.
[Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd#rendering-frozen-documents) explains
that requirement.

```yaml
execute:
  freeze: auto
```

Each render of a PHP document starts a new PHP session. Quarto does not keep a
PHP kernel alive between renders. [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd#quarto)
covers the details.
